app.title: agentoo
app.subtitle: Run Claude agents against your projects.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.empty: No projects yet. Add one above — clone a repository, or point at a folder that already exists on the server.

form.heading: Add a project
form.name: Name
form.sshKeyHint: Needed for a private repository over ssh. Only applies to git@… and ssh:// remotes.
form.sshKeyEmptyHint: No keys yet. If this repository is private, generate one on the SSH keys page and add it to your git host as a deploy key first.
form.folderTip: Only folders in this directory can be added. To bring a project onto the server, copy it here — with scp or rsync, say — then reload this page.
form.emptyHint: Creates an empty git repository in the projects directory. Useful for starting something new with an agent.

delete.confirmClone: Delete "{{name}}" and remove its files from the server?
delete.confirmExisting: Remove "{{name}}"? The folder in the sources directory is yours and will be left alone.

recovery.heading: Setup could not authenticate
recovery.keyExplain: SSH is never anonymous — GitHub and GitLab require a key on their ssh endpoint even for a public repository. Pick a key that has been added to the host as a deploy key, or create one first.
recovery.noKeysYet: No keys yet — generate one, then add it to the host as a deploy key.
recovery.httpsExplain: If the repository is public, https needs no credential at all and is the simpler fix. This rewrites the remote and clears the key.
recovery.manualExplain: Clone it over SSH yourself, where git can prompt you for a passphrase, then check again. Anything already present at the target path is adopted rather than re-cloned.
recovery.checkAgain: I did the manual steps — check again

projects.keyRetryHint: Changing the key does not re-clone.

sshKeys.heading: Your keys
sshKeys.intro: Keys are generated as ed25519 with no passphrase, because the server clones unattended and nobody is there to type one. Only the public half is ever shown or returned by the API — the private key stays on disk, readable only by the service account.
sshKeys.empty: No keys yet. Generate one above if you need to clone a private repository.
sshKeys.deleteConfirm: Delete the key "{{name}}"? Projects using it fall back to ssh defaults.

form.heading: Generate a key
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Becomes the filename. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
form.commentHint: Goes into the key as a label. An email is conventional.

errors.nameChars: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only; must start with a letter or digit

steps.copy: Copy the public key and add it to your git host as a deploy key (GitHub: repo → Settings → Deploy keys).
steps.test: Press Test to confirm the host accepts it.
steps.use: Select the key when adding a project with an ssh remote.

sessions.heading: Sessions
sessions.empty: No sessions yet. Create one above — it gets its own git worktree and branch, so it will not collide with anything else running on this project.
sessions.deleteConfirm: Delete this session? Its worktree is removed, but the branch is kept so the work is not lost.
sessions.notImplemented: Sessions currently reserve a worktree and a branch. Running agents in them, and streaming their output here, is the next piece of work — nothing executes yet.

form.heading: New session
form.title: Title
form.orchestratorHint: The agent that drives this session and delegates to subagents.
form.orchestratorEmpty: No orchestrator agents in the library yet. Add one with role: orchestrator.
form.budgetHint: Optional hard ceiling for the whole session, passed to the SDK. Subagent requests count towards it.
form.notReady: The project has to finish setup first.
